title: Write plain-language summaries of 5 water-safety fact sheets
brief: We publish technical fact sheets about household water treatment (chlorination, solar disinfection, ceramic filtration, boiling, safe storage). The source texts are public WHO guidance. For each of the five methods, write a summary at a 6th-grade reading level, under 200 words, that a community health volunteer could read aloud. Avoid jargon; where a technical term is unavoidable, define it in one clause.
acceptanceCriteria: Five summaries, one per method, each under 200 words
Reading level approximately 6th grade (short sentences, common words)
Each summary ends with one clear 'do this' action
No safety-critical detail from the source guidance is lost or contradicted

title: Clean and deduplicate a public food-bank locations CSV
brief: We aggregated food-bank locations from three public directories into one CSV (name, address, city, state, zip, phone, hours). The merge introduced duplicates with slightly different spellings, inconsistent phone formats, and mixed-case city names. Produce a cleaned CSV: deduplicate rows that refer to the same location, normalize phone numbers to (XXX) XXX-XXXX, title-case city names, and flag rows with missing or unparseable addresses in a new 'needs_review' column instead of deleting them.
acceptanceCriteria: No two rows refer to the same physical location
All phone numbers in (XXX) XXX-XXXX format or blank
Rows with missing/unparseable addresses kept and flagged, not dropped
A short note listing every merge decision that involved judgment

title: Accessibility audit of a small nonprofit website (public URL)
brief: Audit the public marketing site of a small nonprofit (5 pages: home, about, programs, donate, contact) against WCAG 2.1 AA. For each page, list concrete failures (missing alt text, contrast ratios, focus order, form labels, heading structure) with the exact element and a suggested fix. Prioritize the findings: what blocks screen-reader users entirely vs. what degrades the experience.
acceptanceCriteria: Findings organized per page, each with element, WCAG criterion, and suggested fix
Every finding is verifiable from the public site alone
A prioritized top-5 list of fixes with the biggest impact
No speculative findings — only issues actually observed
